body:
Global crypto markets shed $2.27T in aggregate value on August 11, down 1.49% over the past 24 hours, with sentiment registering a Fear & Greed reading of 29 against yesterday's 30, essentially flat and well into fear territory. The mood is cautious but not panicked — volume across all tracked majors came in at $51.5B for the session, which is respectable without being the kind of flush that signals capitulation. BTC dominance held at 56.5% and ETH dominance sits at 10.0%, telling you the market is consolidating around quality rather than chasing risk. The broad narrative is one of digestion: traders are watching macro crosscurrents while the legislative calendar in Washington starts to matter again.

BTC printed $64,031, off 1.90% on the day but up 0.60% on the week, suggesting the selling is orderly rather than structural. The hourly tick of +0.20% hints at stabilization near current levels, but the CoinDesk headline flagging traders eyeing $70,000 next implies the bull case is alive in positioning if not yet in price. Volume of $20.65B is solid for a down day, meaning this isn't a quiet drift lower — there is two-sided activity here. The BIP-110 fork remaining 300 blocks behind BTC and the Luke Dashjr editorial removal are both internal Bitcoin governance stories that carry no immediate price relevance but are worth monitoring for developer sentiment over the medium term. The BTCPay exploit with a $190,000 bounty is a reminder that infrastructure-layer risk is never zero.

ETH fell 2.60% to $1,876.47, underperforming BTC on the day and dragging the altcoin complex with it. Volume of $7.04B was meaningful but ETH's 10.0% dominance figure suggests it is not recovering ground relative to Bitcoin. SOL at $75.66 held up comparatively well, down only 1.70% on the day with a stronger 7-day print of +3.10%, and volume of $1.37B shows active participation. The standout on the day was LINK, which bucked the trend entirely, printing +2.80% to $8.49 with a 7-day gain of +3.80% — a clean divergence that warrants attention given Chainlink's oracle infrastructure relevance to the "new blockchain rail for a $2T asset class" story referenced in the CoinDesk headline. ADA was the ugliest name in the book, down 5.00% to $0.188374 with a 7-day loss of 3.20%, and XRP shed 3.30% to exactly $1.005, now down 6.50% on the week — both look technically soft with no near-term catalyst visible. BNB at $602.43 was the relative outperformer among larger caps, losing only 0.30% on the day.

Macro context is doing the heavy lifting here. The White House vowing to get CLARITY legislation across the finish line in September is a concrete regulatory timeline that the market has not fully priced, and the SEC scheduling a meeting to propose Reg Crypto framework for digital asset offerings is directionally constructive but creates near-term uncertainty around compliance costs and eligible assets. South Korea's decision to lower the Travel Rule threshold for crypto transfers tightens the compliance net in a major retail market and could weigh on offshore exchange volumes. On the structural side, Decta exploring stablecoin-enabled treasury settlement and the broader tokenization theme implied by the $2T asset class rail headline are medium-term tailwinds that need price discovery to mature. Rates and broader macro data are not specifically cited in today's inputs, so the read here is that crypto is trading on its own internal catalysts for now rather than reacting to a major macro print.

Looking ahead, the September legislative deadline on CLARITY is the single biggest calendar item to track — a credible passage path would likely be the catalyst that takes BTC toward the $70,000 level traders are already discussing. The SEC Reg Crypto proposal meeting is a binary risk: a well-scoped framework accelerates institutional product development, while an overly restrictive draft could compress multiples across the DeFi and token-issuance stack, which would hurt names like UNI at $3.95 and ADA hardest. Watch LINK for confirmation of the tokenization theme; if that trade continues to outperform on further risk-off days it signals genuine fundamental rotation rather than noise. ADA and XRP need to stabilize quickly or the 7-day losses accelerate into what would be technically meaningful breakdowns. The BTCPay exploit is worth monitoring for contagion into merchant-adoption narratives, and any escalation in the BIP-110 governance dispute could introduce developer uncertainty at exactly the wrong time in the cycle.
